conventions.axes: Y-up, right-handed; camera looks down -Z by default; ground is the XZ plane at y = 0
conventions.lightIntensity: three.js physical units (directional/hemisphere/ambient: lux-like; spot/point: candela, decay 2)
conventions.easing: named functions from kit/time.js `ease` (formulas in references/kit-api.md)
conventions.camera: fov is vertical field of view in degrees (three.js convention); sensor-agnostic

style.name: Pendulum Wave
style.description: A classic pendulum-wave demonstration on a bright, cool-white bench: a row of 15 large glossy balls, saturated rainbow by index, hangs on V-strings from a curved wooden beam carried by two A-frames, each pendulum a little shorter than the last. Pendulum k completes (N + k) swings in one cycle, so released together from a wooden plank they drift into a travelling snake wave, split into groups, look like chaos, and then all return to one line at the same instant, where the plank catches them. Everything is a closed form of t (wave.js): angles, string lengths (from the periods), motion-trail ghosts (the same formula at earlier times), a lamp on the bench under each ball that flashes at its centre crossing, and one pitched bar note per crossing, so the sound goes from a chord strike to a ripple and back to a unison. A planned clock can freeze the motion: a camera flash, and the frozen positions fly down into an overlay 'fingerprint' card.
motion: Pendulum k: angle = A_k cos(2 pi (N + k) tau / T); A_k = asin(reach / L_k) so every ball leaves the same straight plank.
String lengths come from the periods: L_k = Lmin ((N + n - 1) / (N + k))^2.
tau(t) is a planned clock (piecewise-linear rate, closed form and invertible): it can slow to a freeze-frame and resume.
Trails are the same formula at earlier tau, scaled by the clock rate, so they vanish in a freeze. Nothing accumulates.
At tau = T every ball is back at the plank with zero speed; the plank rises and holds them: start state = end state.
Camera: one move per beat, locked during holds; end-on for the snake, high front for the frozen patterns.

notes.mechanism: wave.js: pendulum k makes (16 + k) swings per cycle; angle = A_k cos(2 pi (16 + k) tau / T); L_k ~ 1 / (16 + k)^2; tau(t) = planned clock (freezes); T = tau(catchAt), so all 15 are back on the plank at 13.0 s.
notes.plan: T = 10.35 s of clock, 345 centre crossings (one note + lamp flash each), lengths 0.90..3.16 m
notes.numbers: no data shown; the fingerprint cards plot the frozen ball displacements from the plan
